title: I built a Roleplay AI that grew too fast, and we had to shut it down. Here is why I am starting over.
author: MagiNeko
selftext:
Hey, quick story.

In 2023 I was on a small dev team for a Character AI / RP platform. It grew way faster than we were ready for - \~300k users in about 4 months. Sounds great on paper. In reality, we basically lived in "scale the servers, put out fires, repeat" mode.

The worst part wasn't even the scaling. It was keeping long-form stories coherent while the user count exploded. Context memory became a black hole. We spent more time tweaking infra costs than improving the actual RP experience.

Eventually, the content went one direction, investors wanted a different direction, and the whole thing fell apart. We shut it down.

I'm not naming the old platform. It wasn't a solo project, and I'm not trying to farm hype off the name.

Since then I've been building business AI tools, but I kept coming back to RP. I feel like most bots today are still just... chat. I want something that can actually run a scene - pacing, atmosphere, time/place, light RPG state - instead of mirroring whatever tone the user throws at it.

So I'm rebuilding from scratch as a personal side project

[Less generic chat, more scene pacing + time\/location state.](https://preview.redd.it/mt9tn3z6lidg1.png?width=1886&format=png&auto=webp&s=5b7dbf289055fd69fb9e16002e2e062b54676344)

[The AI should know your role + relationship in the scenario.](https://preview.redd.it/72ulgfx2lidg1.png?width=2010&format=png&auto=webp&s=ca3761e496276febc93d380855f1b62dc92be41d)

[Aiming for a library of worlds, not a wall of bots.](https://preview.redd.it/sye47eyjlidg1.png?width=2400&format=png&auto=webp&s=d6858c09c34df31bd6f2a74c3883f1b046c22ac6)

I'm keeping the beta small (around 100 people) because I don't want a repeat of 2023 where rapid growth dictated every decision. I mainly just want honest feedback to help get the pacing right.

If you're into narrative-heavy RP and want to help test an engine built for immersion, I'd love to have you on board.

I’ll be posting updates and opening the beta access here: r/MagiVerseAI

replies.author: MagiNeko

Thanks for signing up and for the kind words. Really appreciate it.

comments.author: AreaCoinMan
comments.body: You are worrying me tbh... I have a fast growing AI TTRPG platform too. It's [https://macer.ai](https://macer.ai) and the usage is booming lately.

comments.author: RagingCain
comments.body:
I am literally starting my own thing focused solely first on designing the ML context window as a platform for gaming.

As I am new to both game design and ML, I am leaning deep in my back end engineering experience. I have a lot of ideas of what could work for the lifecycle of a video game, that needs an essentially infinite context window. The journey for me is how close can I emulate that experience, without costs, generative quality issues, or most importantly performance degradation.

My text generation prototype has done well, but it's only a matter of time before it fails and I am trying to figure out how to accept it will fall apart at some point but to still give the player agency to self-remediate... without destroying immersion entirely.

comments.author: HerbertGoon
comments.body: I thought the title meant it was becoming sentient. Grew too fast and ye had to stop it before it took over.

comments.author: Original-Fabulous
comments.body:
In my opinion, you’re not describing a better chat bot but essentially a single-player “game” of sorts. A game where users get to create the explicit game states such as scene, time, place, tension, goals etc, but also stats to track, pacing rules, player verbs even.

Treat the LLM as one system inside it, not the product, then let the LLM express that state rather than invent it.

comments.author: SereneAlps3789
comments.body: Can you give any details on monthly cost of previous RP project?

comments.author: AdAccurate9264
comments.body: Building something like this sounds like a huge challenge but also really exciting. Getting the pacing and immersion right is crucial, especially when trying to create a believable world for users. Have you looked into alternatives like tronovex? It might offer some features that could help with the long-form storytelling aspect. Keeping a small beta sounds smart too, especially after your last experience. Feedback from a smaller group can really shape the direction without the chaos of rapid growth. Can't wait to see how it all turns out!
